candidate.prompt_text: Talk about a film or story character you like. Say the character’s name and describe him or her in a few words.
suggested_ideas: what the character looks like or is like
what the character does in the film or story

evaluation_guide.expected_content: A short personal description of one film or story character, with simple details and a clear reason for liking the character.
evaluation_guide.key_points: Names a character; gives at least 1–2 simple descriptive details; says why the character is liked; produces common content words clearly enough for stress to be heard.
evaluation_guide.acceptable_responses: Any understandable answer about a real or fictional character from a film or story is acceptable, including animated, literary, or school-text characters. The student may use simple sentences and basic vocabulary.
evaluation_guide.off_topic_examples: Talking only about the actor instead of the character; giving a summary of the whole film with no focus on one character; discussing games, sports, or music with no link to a film or story character.
evaluation_guide.scoring_hints: For word stress, listen for stress in common two- and three-syllable words such as 'character', 'friendly', 'beautiful', 'interesting', and film or story titles if said. Reward clear stressed syllables even if other pronunciation features are imperfect.
evaluation_guide.common_mistakes: Flat stress across all syllables; stressing the wrong syllable in common words; listing adjectives too quickly to hear stress; giving memorized content with unclear articulation; not naming a character.

candidate.prompt_text: Describe a scene in a film or story that you remember well.

evaluation_guide.expected_content: A simple description of one memorable scene, including place, people, action, and a brief reason it is memorable.
evaluation_guide.key_points: Mentions one specific scene; gives basic details about place or people; explains the action simply; says why the scene is remembered; produces some stressed multi-syllable words clearly.
evaluation_guide.acceptable_responses: Any understandable scene from a film, cartoon, play, or written story is acceptable. The scene may be happy, funny, sad, or exciting, as long as the response stays appropriate and clear.
evaluation_guide.off_topic_examples: Describing the whole film or story with no single scene; talking only about favorite actors or music; giving an unrelated real-life event instead of a scene from a film or story.
evaluation_guide.scoring_hints: Listen for word stress in words like 'remember', 'exciting', 'suddenly', 'beautiful', 'dangerous', or other descriptive vocabulary chosen by the student. Give credit when stressed syllables help intelligibility.
evaluation_guide.common_mistakes: Stress placed on the wrong syllable in frequent adjectives and adverbs; unclear scene description because of too many disconnected words; speaking so softly or fast that stress cannot be judged; not identifying any scene.
